item.title: European soccer's governing body flips sport upside down with boycott of FIFA, future World Cups
item.description: UEFA accuses FIFA of selling football's soul through its FIFA Forward Enterprise plan, with reports of a European boycott of the 2030 World Cup.
item.content:encoded:
The 2030 World Cup may be missing many of soccer's global powerhouses, with UEFA's announcement that it will be boycotting FIFA.

FIFA, the sport's global governing body, recently published proposed details of a company titled FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) that would allow private investors to buy shares in the World Cup. FFE is being formed to run the governing body's commercial rights and event operations, and the infusion of private capital into FIFA and all of its competitions, including the World Cup. This would not be in the sport's best interest according to UEFA, European soccer’s 55-member governing body.

UEFA released a statement on Thursday bluntly explaining that its national associations will not participate in FIFA competitions.

The decision comes on the heels of FIFA sending letters or proposals to its 211 member nations with a deadline of Sept. 19 for member associations to get on board, with 75% support needed to change bylaws. FIFA states that it would remain a not-for-profit organization – as it is recognized in Switzerland – while FFE would be a controlled commercial subsidiary.

FIFA EYES WORLD CUP FORMAT EXPANSION FROM 48 TO 64 TEAMS: SHOULD THE US BE THE PERMANENT HOST?

FIFA president Gianni Infantino explained that private capital infusion would see members receive $10 billion in total funds, which equates to approximately $40 million per association. Infantino is also promising smaller federations would see development payouts go from $8 million to $20 million through 2030.

UEFA and its 55 member associations "unanimously and unequivocally reject" FIFA's proposal.

"The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies," UEFA's statement read. "It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.

"It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA’s duty as the custodian of world football."

Furthermore, UEFA's statement explained that the game of soccer is not for sale.

"Europe’s position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation," the statement continued.

"As a result of today’s discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership.

"Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination."

When reached for comment by Fox News Digital about the development of FFE and reports of UEFA's boycott of FIFA, the organization shared the FAQ section of the FIFA Forward Enterprise published on its official website.

MAURICIO POCHETTINO NEARING NEW DEAL TO STAY AS UNITED STATES MANAGER THROUGH 2030 FIFA WORLD CUP

This boycott flips the global game upside down.

Both the men's and women's World Cup would take place without European national teams, including the likes of England, France, Germany, Spain, Portugal, and Belgium. The European Championships and Champions League, both controlled by UEFA, would continue to take place.

According to the New York Post, Thrive Eternal is expected to lead the investor group if the FFE proposal is passed and take on up to a 20% stake for more than $4.2 billion. Thrive is an American venture capital firm founded by President Donald Trump's son-in-law Joshua Kushner.

The men's 2030 FIFA World Cup will be jointly hosted by Spain, Morocco, and Portugal. The 2027 Women's World Cup will take place in Brazil.

item.title: Dolphins not going to 'throw in the towel and just rebuild' but that comes with higher expectations
item.description: Jeff Halfley rejects the rebuild narrative even after Miami traded Jaylen Waddle and Minkah Fitzpatrick and released Bradley Chubb this year.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins are in a rebuilding year, and anyone with eyes can see that based on the offseason coaching, personnel and roster moves. But head coach Jeff Halfley doesn't want to hear that.

Say that.

Admit that.

"I don't know how you can have a conversation with a competitive player or a competitive coach, and have it sit right with them, where they were just going to say I was going to rebuild this year," Halfley said on Thursday. "...It's just not the mentality of any competitor who's made it to this level or any coach that's made it to this level.

"I mean, whether it's practice or whether it's a drill, I think we all want to win it. And in our mindset is, we need to get better. We need to develop. And everything that we do is going to be about competing to get better throughout the process and we want to win.

" So I just don't think any player or any coach is going to sit here and say, 'I'm just going to throw in the towel and just rebuild.' So that's probably why no one's hearing that. I think if you had a group of players saying that, then I think we got the wrong players."

This is a message Halfley has been delivering within the organization throughout the offseason. It's a message staffers and even the public relations department has for months been privately sharing with anyone who will listen.

The Dolphins don't want to say they're rebuilding.

Even though, you know, they're rebuilding.

We know they are because a team that wants to win now doesn't move on from good players, especially if they're young.

But the Dolphins did that in trading three-time 1,000-yard receiver Jaylen Waddle to Denver even though he would be their best wideout now. They did that in trading five-time Pro Bowl player Minkah Fitzpatrick even though he would be the best safety on their roster now.

They did that in releasing Bradley Chubb after he led the team in sacks last season.

BRONCOS ACQUIRE WADDLE AS NEW PIECE FOR SUPER BOWL RUN

And we get it. The Dolphins made tactical moves to clean up the salary cap.

But the strategic objective of that was to be competitive next year and maybe be very good in a couple of years.

This year? The club signed or re-signed over a dozen players to one-year contracts. They added players like veteran Josh Uche for the short-term to maybe, hopefully, fill a gap until the team finds a better pass-rush answer.

"He's a guy that's tasted success in this league. And I think he's probably been humbled and motivated by last year, you know, being inactive for a bunch," Halfley said. "But seeing a guy, like a lot of guys that we have on this roster right now, he is at the point of his career where it's a prove-it year.

"It's prove-it year for himself. It's a chance for him to say, I can still do this."

Halfley could easily say that about a dozen players on his roster who have either never contributed in the NFL or want to show they can still contribute after failing to do so recently.

And amid this reality, his message is the Dolphins want to win – as in now.

But here's one thing posture brings: A different evaluation.

If Halfley, and the entire organization by extension, keep insisting this is not a rebuilding year, then expectations change.

It's acceptable for a rebuilding team to win only four, five, six games. It's a rebuild, after all.

But a team that states 2026 is much more than "just a rebuild," must do more. Fans should expect more. Teams like that need to win more than they lose or they've failed in the eyes of some fans.

So this gets tricky.

Halfley, in the first year of his first NFL head coaching job, has to tread carefully to keep expectations high for his players while not raising them and hopes too high outside the team.

item.title: Federal judge blocks DOJ access to NJ voter rolls amid statewide controversy
item.description: District Judge Zahid Quraishi blocked the Justice Department from accessing New Jersey's unredacted voter registration list, citing privacy concerns.
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge in New Jersey blocked the Justice Department from gaining access to the state's unredacted voter rolls on Wednesday.

District Judge Zahid Quraishi, a Biden appointee, ruled that handing over the rolls could give rise to privacy concerns for voters. The ruling is the latest defeat for President Donald Trump's administration after the DOJ sued Utah, Oklahoma, Kentucky, West Virginia and New Jersey for access to their voter rolls earlier this year.

The administration argued that Title III of the Civil Rights Act granted federal authorities access to the lists, but Quraishi disagreed.

TRUMP-APPOINTED FEDERAL JUDGE TOSSES DOJ LAWSUIT SEEKING ARIZONA VOTER DATA

"The plain text of Title III applies only to records ‘which come into’ election officers’ ‘possession’ and thus does not extend to New Jersey’s computerized VRL [voter registration list] – a document the State itself created," Quraishi wrote.

Quraishi's ruling also comes amid a statewide controversy related to noncitizen voting in New Jersey.

New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill admitted last week that a "serious software error" led to the mistaken registration of roughly 6,600 noncitizens through the state's Motor Vehicle System, while the company that provides the identity-related security services denied any wrongdoing.

DEMOCRATS CONCEDE NJ VOTER-ROLL FAILURE WAS ‘HORRIBLE’ — BUT REJECT BROADER FRAUD FEARS

"In New Jersey, we absolutely need to have accountability for what happened," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said of the incident. "It was just horrible. There was a big problem with that computer problem that they had. We need to try to address that going forward."

Sherrill said she immediately ordered an investigation after the error was discovered and that the state's Division of Elections is removing ineligible voters from the rolls. She said fewer than 400 of those improperly registered cast ballots.

Reports also surfaced this week that roughly 75,000 noncitizens had been summoned for jury duty through state databases, according to multiple reports, broadening the controversy beyond the Motor Vehicle Commission and prompting additional Republican calls for a wider investigation.

Fox News' Charles Creitz contributed to this report.
